claims.text: Adding a controlled, low concentration of tungsten to the HEA intermediate layer will promote nanoscale tungsten-rich secondary phases.
The tungsten-rich secondary phases will be nanoscale precipitates integrated within the HEA matrix.
The tungsten-rich precipitates will be coherently bonded to the HEA matrix.
Tungsten-rich precipitates will provide localized heat-conduction paths with higher electron mobility.
Tungsten-rich precipitates will provide localized heat-conduction paths with higher phonon mobility.
The localized conduction paths created by the precipitates will enhance the overall heat-transfer capability of the HEA.
The HEA matrix has characteristic sluggish diffusion.
The HEA matrix possesses intrinsic strength that can preserve structural stability during thermal, mechanical, and radiation loading.
Tungsten doping could increase thermal conductivity by approximately 10–20% relative to the undoped HEA.
The tungsten-doped HEA will maintain mechanical properties comparable to those of the undoped baseline.
Current undoped HEA intermediate layers have moderate thermal conductivity and acceptable structural integrity.
Temperatures up to approximately 600°C are typical of intermediate-layer operation in plasma-facing reactor environments.
The proposed thermal and mechanical benefits should persist under cyclic thermal, radiation, and mechanical loading up to approximately 600°C.
The intervention may cease to be effective at significantly higher temperatures or under loading more extreme than typical plasma-facing service conditions.
Long-term radiation exposure may affect the stability of the tungsten-rich precipitates.
